mcqs.learning_point: Recognise squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombi and trapezia
mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has four equal sides and four right angles. Which type of quadrilateral is it?
mcqs.explanation: A shape with four equal sides and four right angles satisfies the definition of a square. A rectangle also has right angles but its sides are not all equal; a rhombus has equal sides but not necessarily right angles; a trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand relationships among different quadrilateral classes
mcqs.question: If a quadrilateral is both a rectangle and a rhombus, which specific quadrilateral does it become?
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and all angles right; a rhombus has all sides equal. When both conditions hold, the figure has equal sides and right angles, which is the definition of a square. The other options do not satisfy both properties.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a quadrilateral?

options.C: A shape with two pairs of parallel sides
options.D: A shape with all sides equal

mcqs.explanation: A quadrilateral is any polygon that has exactly four sides (and consequently four vertices and four interior angles). Option A describes a triangle, C describes a parallelogram, and D describes a rhombus or square, which are specific types of quadrilaterals, not the general definition.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify sides, vertices and angles of quadrilaterals
mcqs.question: How many sides, vertices, and interior angles does any quadrilateral have?
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a quadrilateral has four straight sides, each meeting at a vertex, giving four vertices. The interior angles at those vertices also total four. The other options give counts that belong to polygons with different numbers of sides.

mcqs.question: Which quadrilateral has all four sides equal but does not necessarily have right angles?
mcqs.explanation: A rhombus is defined by having all four sides equal; its angles can be acute, obtuse, or right. A square also has all sides equal but additionally requires all angles to be right angles, making it a special case of a rhombus. Rectangles have opposite sides equal, not all four, and trapeziums have only one pair of parallel sides.

mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has one pair of opposite angles equal and the other pair also equal, but none of the angles are right angles. Which type of quadrilateral is it?
mcqs.explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles are supplementary. The condition that none of the angles are right angles excludes squares and rectangles. Trapeziums do not generally have opposite angles equal, and a kite has a pair of equal adjacent angles, not opposite ones.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombi and trapezia
mcqs.question: Which quadrilateral has both pairs of opposite sides parallel and all four sides equal?
mcqs.explanation: A square satisfies both conditions: opposite sides are parallel (as in any parallelogram) and all four sides are equal. A rectangle has opposite sides equal but not all four sides equal; a rhombus has all sides equal but angles are not necessarily right; a generic parallelogram meets the parallel condition but not the equal‑sides condition.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand relationships among different quadrilateral classes
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between rectangles and parallelograms?

options.C: Rectangles and parallelograms are unrelated classes
options.D: Only squares belong to both classes

mcqs.explanation: A rectangle meets all the criteria of a parallelogram (both pairs of opposite sides parallel) and adds the condition that all angles are right. Therefore every rectangle is a specific type of parallelogram. Not every parallelogram is a rectangle because its angles need not be right. Hence options B, C, and D are incorrect.
